scenario: A space-medicine fellowship admits candidates who have deep expertise in radiation biology OR in human-factors engineering. Both specialisms are independent in the applicant pool; OR-gate admission produces a within-cohort negative correlation.

data.description: Population base rates and OR-gate selection mechanism

values.selection_rule: OR gate: selected if (radiation biology expertise) OR (human-factors engineering expertise)

question: (a) Derive P(selected) from the OR-gate model. (b) Compute P(radiation_biology | ¬human_factors, selected) and explain why it equals 1. (c) Compute P(radiation_biology | human_factors, selected) and show it equals P(radiation_biology). (d) Quantify the induced conditional correlation direction and explain why it is a selection artefact rather than a genuine population relationship between radiation biology expertise and human-factors engineering expertise.

ground_truth.explanation: Under OR-gate selection a candidate who lacks human-factors engineering expertise must possess radiation biology expertise to be admitted — hence P(radiation_biology|¬human_factors,sel)=1.0. A candidate who already has human-factors engineering expertise is admitted regardless of radiation biology expertise, so P(radiation_biology|human_factors,sel)=P(radiation_biology)=0.37. The gap (1.0 vs 0.37) creates a negative within-selected correlation that is purely a collider-selection artefact.

naive_answer: The negative correlation between radiation biology expertise and human-factors engineering expertise observed among selected candidates reflects a genuine trade-off between these traits in the domain.
naive_trap: The negative correlation is entirely a Berkson collider artefact produced by the OR-gate admission rule; the two traits are independent in the full population.
reasoning_trace: (1) P(sel)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A)P(B)=0.37+0.53-0.37×0.53=0.7039. (2) Among candidates without human-factors engineering expertise: only those with radiation biology expertise are selected → P(radiation_biology|¬human_factors,sel)=1.0. (3) Among candidates with human-factors engineering expertise: selected regardless of radiation biology expertise → P(radiation_biology|human_factors,sel)=P(radiation_biology)=0.37. (4) Within-selected: knowing ¬human_factors raises P(radiation_biology) from 0.37 to 1.0 → negative conditional correlation despite population independence.
python_verification:
pA,pB = 0.37,0.53
pSel = pA+pB-pA*pB
assert abs(pSel-0.7039)<0.005, f'pSel={pSel}'
pA_notB_sel = pA*(1-pB)/(pA*(1-pB))   # =1.0 by definition
assert abs(pA_notB_sel-1.0)<1e-9
pA_B_sel = pA*pB/pB                    # =pA by definition
assert abs(pA_B_sel-0.37)<1e-9
assert pA_notB_sel > pA_B_sel, 'negative collider correlation confirmed'
